name: GARMENT STORAGE CABINET
desc: Class 100 Vertical Laminar Flow Cleanroom Garment Storage Cabinet engineered to maintain sterile conditions in high-compliance cleanrooms. Features a dual-compartment internal layout fabricated from high-grade SS304 or 316, driven by a two-stage filtration network.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS GARMENT STORAGE CABINET is a Class 100 / ISO Class 5 vertical laminar flow cleanroom garment storage system engineered to preserve the sterility and particulate integrity of cleanroom apparel. It employs a two-stage filtration matrix: a washable primary pre-filter captures macroscopic dust, while a micro-glass fiber HEPA filter removes 99.997% of airborne particles down to 0.3 microns, delivering a uniform vertical downflow at 0.45 ± 0.05 m/s that continuously scrubs the internal storage space. An automated UV germicidal disinfection lamp, interlocked with door-open switches, provides surface decontamination of stored gowns, coveralls, hoods, boots, and gloves. Doctors, B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and chemists rely on this cabinet to maintain aseptic conditions before handling strong acids (e.g., HCl, HNO3), volatile organic compounds (e.g., toluene, xylene), microbial cultures, cell lines, and performing critical assays such as sterility testing, endotoxin (LAL) testing, and PCR. It supports compliance with ISO 14644-1 Class 5, EU GMP Annex 1 Grade A/B, USP <797>, and ASTM F838 standards for cleanroom garment management.
sop: Ensure the cabinet is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz single-phase supply and switch ON the main power isolator.
Check the differential pressure gauge (if fitted) to confirm the HEPA filter pressure drop is within the manufacturer's specified range.
Press the "SET" button once to access the controller setpoint mode.
Use the "UP" and "DOWN" arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., UV disinfection cycle duration or airflow velocity setpoint).
Press "SET" again to lock the value and return to the normal operating display.
Before loading, ensure the UV lamp is OFF and the glass doors are fully closed for at least 5 minutes to allow any residual ozone to dissipate.
Sanitize the interior surfaces and shelves with 70% isopropyl alcohol or a validated sporicidal disinfectant using a lint-free wipe.
Load cleanroom garments: hang coveralls and frocks on the dedicated rods, place folded hoods, boots, and gloves on the removable shelves without overcrowding.
Close the stainless steel framed glass doors and verify the self-closing hinges seal completely.
Activate the UV germicidal disinfection cycle as per the laboratory schedule, ensuring no personnel are exposed to UV radiation.
Record the airflow velocity, UV cycle time, and any deviations in the equipment logbook.

Safety Warning: Never open the glass doors while the UV lamp is active; UV-C radiation can cause severe skin burns and eye damage. Always verify the lamp is off and allow adequate ventilation before accessing the cabinet, and never store chemical containers, biological samples, or flammable materials inside.
